Explorada for the River is a research campaign in the Beyond, which in 1774 was headed by Erwin Sofia Jessica Origin. (Erwin Origin) From this storyline (the chapters of Arrow) begins the story of Erwin in the novel Arrow, Coin, Spark. The campaign was conceived as an honorable reference to the obstinate heir, and ended with a discovery that turned the history of the empire.

Exploding as an establishment

Explorers in the old days were called trips beyond the borders of the state. Half a millennium ago, when the empire was small, the emperors allowed the lords to attach new lands to it. Half of the conquered became lord's laziness, the rest went to the Crown. By the time of the novel, the entire continent of Polaris had long been under the rule of the Crown, so the very idea of the exploit seemed to Erwin nonsense. Only the Beyond remained unexplored - a huge, wild and cold continent, connected to Polaris by a narrow isthmus, which is covered by the Crystal Mountains. Maps of those places did not exist, and the only settlement on the isthmus was the settlement of Spot.

Lady Karen in the collectible edition of Arrow, Coin, Spark tells of later attempts. (Arrow, Coin, Spark (Collector's Edition)) In the middle of the XVIII century, in the era of the expansion of borders, expeditions of the northern lords, the Southern Way, the Crown and even Fais and Minnis went to the Beyond by land and sea. They were lured by the belief that somewhere there was the Holy Way - a descent into the underworld of the gods, from where the Forebears came. Half of the expeditions disappeared, the other came back with losses, and the survivors went crazy and talked about unprecedented monsters. The educated society decided that there was a natural “source of madness” in the Beyond, and the trips deep into the mainland stopped. Relatively safe recognized strip from the Crystal Mountains to the River. Survivors brought with them superstitions such as those followed by Coleman, and Karen notes that his magical thinking was more appropriate than Erwin’s sanity in Beyond. (Colemon)

According to the law of Constantine, published in the XIII century, in any campaign beyond the known borders of the empire should participate a person directly serving the Crown. Therefore, an imperial observer was included in the detachment.

Background

In March 1774, Erwin returned from the capital to the First Winter for Iona's sister's wedding to Vittor Shayland. He outlined his plan to his father: to support the reforms of Emperor Adrian in exchange for generous concessions to the Crown. The Duke of Desmond considered it a trade of loyalty close to treason. He then sent his son to the graveyard. Erwin had to cross the Crystal Mountains, get supplies in Spot that would drive the ship, and then cross the Soft Fields and the Shadow Forest. According to available information, about three hundred miles from the mountains, in the depths of the Forest of Shadows, flows a large river without a name, which legends call simply the River. It should have found a place for a spark dam.

Erwin tried to argue: for a whole century in the empire built only ten dams, and in the Beyond would have to lay the rails and build a city for the builders. The campaign was to take several months: Erwin would return to the capital only in the fall, when the betrothal of Adrian would be behind, that is, he would lose the summer season in the capital, when the fate of reforms and the imperial marriage was decided. The father remained adamant: upon his return, his son was to live in the First Winter, and Desmond himself was going to go to the capital in the summer and apologize to the emperor for his son's actions. Desmond also reported that the emperor approved of his plan. According to the later reconstruction of Mark, Adrian agreed on the condition that Erwin lead the campaign.

In addition to the dam, the campaign had a second task. Desmond hoped that through the Crystal Mountains it would be possible to lay a rail road, and separately instructed the mechanic to mark the area. Before the captain of the kairs, the duke set his own task - to move to the east until there is room for a spark shop. Coming out of his father's office, Erwin collided at the door with the mechanic Luis Maria, a future companion, and suspected that he was eavesdropping.

Composition of the squad

A group of forty people spoke after the wedding celebrations.

  • Keira. The core of the unit consisted of eleven dedicated northern knights, each with two greys, foot soldiers-servants. They were commanded by Captain Theobart, the sixth son of a poor cyre, who received a cape at fifteen, and at twenty became the squire of Desmond himself. Erwin knew him from childhood and believed that his father put the captain to him as a nanny. Among the kires were Jemis Lilliday with Grey Shepherd Sagittarius, Oswald, Frederick, Matthew, Donnell, Gilbert, Martin, and Hayvis.
  • Baron Philip Doris Laura Lawfert is an imperial observer in a scarlet camsol with gold veneers. All the way, he scolded Erwin with vulgar stories about his love affairs and persistently called him a “young man.”
  • Luis Maria of Otmeli was an imperial mechanic of the second guild, cartographer and chronicler of the campaign. (Louis Maria) When his horse disappeared, he was riding a donkey.
  • Doctor Filden and Tommy, Erwin's denizen, who had previously served as a Grey at Desmond's for fifteen years. (In early media outlets, Tommy is explicitly referred to as "Lord Erwin's Greeting.")
  • Horses. Erwin, like the three kire, took two horses: the raven stallion Rain and the nervous toy mare Leocanthus.
  • Conductors. In Spot, an old hunter Coleman, a grumbling and superstitious connoisseur, will be hired, and in the guise of a fourteen-year-old Kid hunter, a tireless kid who said every night: "It was a good day, ah!" (Colemon; Kid)

Explorada

The Crystal Mountains (April)

On the sixth day of the journey, in a hurry to the head of the column, Erwin knocked down a Grey Buck with his horse. The boy fell off the slope and broke his leg. Buck’s owner, Kair Jemis, wanted to leave a cripple in the squad, so that he would then “work”. Erwin took the blame and ordered the wounded man to be sent home under his guard. Jemis began to argue in front of witnesses, and then Captain Theobart himself ordered him to obey. Thus, the captain, wanting to help, undermined the authority of the lord: it turned out that the Kairs obeyed not Erwin, but Theobart.

Erwin caught a cold, and the soldiers nicknamed him "the babysitter." The map, which turned out to be a collection of inaccuracies, he began to draw himself. At night on the glacier Podol Servants a hundred steps from the camp passed an avalanche. In the morning, Erwin put his hand to the snow wall and thanked Agatha the Radiant for saving him.

Spot

At the end of April, the unit arrived at Border Spot. The inhabitants of the village, red-haired and curly-nosed descendants of several families, built houses from stones brought by the mountain river Lydyanka. Elder Howard Katrina William took for the ducal son of the discharged Baron Philip, and Erwin had to correct him. The elder described the Soft Fields: a swamp about two hundred miles wide that no one could get around, and crossing it with great luck takes six days. Erwin hired guides, promising twenty agat each, although the locals did not earn so much in a year.

At the feast, Gray Jemis Hank Seaman quarreled with the village guy because of his bride. Erwin shouted to Jemis to stop, but did not have time: Kair, just looking at the lord, with one stroke of the sword cut off the guy's hand to the elbow. Then he was surprised, as if he thought that the lord himself wanted to teach the insolent. Erwin interrupted the feast and told the doctor to help the wounded. When the schooner from the Belomorye with the coat of arms of the Origins came, Erwin waited in vain for letters from his father. Seeing how scarce the duke's gift to the village was, he gave the inhabitants of Spot half of the brought supplies. Theobart coldly warned that starvation would not make the unit turn: it had enough hunters, and the Duke's order would be carried out anyway.

Soft Fields (May)

Soft Fields turned out to be a huge swamp, tightened by a floating network of grass-nets. It was possible to walk only on yellow shallows, and pure black water meant death. Kayra Frederick was bitten by a snake-snake. On the shoal, the detachment met a fan - an armored horned beast larger than a bull. The rain did not want to go to the side, and Erwin, without abandoning him, jumped into the saddle and took the beast out of the way. The fang killed one of the donkeys, and Theobart lured the monster to a deep place, where it fell through the net and drowned. In the evening, a rainstorm caught the squad on the way to the island, and Erwin fell through the network into the quagmire. There were only fifty yards left to the island, but on the bottom, through the hedge, he and Kid, two kairs and Tommy had to wade for more than an hour.

Erwin found a poisonous widow snake in his bed, and she was killed by Jemis. The investigation showed that the snake for the sake of poison for arrows caught Kid and carelessly tied the bag. At the same time it was revealed that Jemis was mocking the mechanic: he put thorns under his saddle and a dead badger in a blanket. Under northern law, the commoner who endangered the lord deserved to be executed, but Erwin spared the Kid, citing that he had saved him on the first night. Jemis, according to Erwin, was waiting for the execution to once again see the weakness of the Lord.

Contrary to the advice of Theobart, Erwin listened to the conductors and did not go around the site with "bad air" - swamp gas. Gray Red did not put out the fire, the gas broke out, and the fire engulfed half a mile of swamps. Erwin, along with Oswald and Louis, shot down the flames with raincoats and lost consciousness from the smoke. Red drowned.

Mutiny in the swamp

When Erwin awoke, he overheard the kair council with Kid's help. While Theobart was in intelligence, Jemis and his associates decided to remove the lord from command and send him to the First Winter as a prisoner. Erwin went out to the fire and reminded each kair of his own story. He told Jemis that his sword could only be obtained by force. Erwin then laid his hands with a blade behind his back, leaving his chest open:

Make your choice, Kyle. If you want to kill me, now is the time.”

Frederick and another kair stood next to the lord, and Jemis, the hereditary Earl of Lilliday, threw away the sword and kneeled. Erwin did not execute him, but tore his cape off him, stripped him of his kair rank and drove him out of the squad, allowing him to take only a knife and a hunting bow. Hank the Sailor is gone. The accomplices of Jemis, Matthew and Donnell, Erwin did not punish. All he said to Theobart was that Jemis rebelled and was punished, and the case was hushed up.

River (end of May - beginning of June)

A week after the swamp, the detachment reached the River, about three hundred and eighty miles from the border of the empire. The river was a quarter of a mile wide, full of water and black, and the east bank it washed into a three-hundred-foot creek. Erwin immediately realized that the dam could not be built here. Louis explained to the others: in this flow, you first need to dig a bypass, and granite will have to be taken from the Crystal Mountains. In the evenings, Colemon told the terrible legends of Zarechye: about the glow in the sky and the knock from behind the River, about walking trees, about man-made bumps with human heads on boar bodies and about the bites of oxen. Because of the river, according to him, no one returned.

On June 3, the scouts reported that the River was as wide as fifty miles upstream, and the Soft Fields were close to it. The task was formally exhausted, and Philip Lawfert offered to return. Later, Erwin admitted to himself that the decisive reason was the dislike of the observer: to agree with Philip he disliked. He ordered the rafts to be built and moved to the east, "until I order otherwise."

Across the River (June 6–7)

On June 6, the unit crossed without incident with the help of an island with willows. The conductors remained on the west bank. Erwin paid them off and gave them two letters to be sent by ship from Spot. He informed his father that the unit had lost one man, that Jemis was stripped of his cloak and that the River was unsuitable for the dam. He wrote four letters to his sister.

On the east bank, the scouts found a dried corpse under the gum. The skeleton was covered with a gray crust, the grass and bark around turned to dust. There were leather pants and boots on the dead man, which seemed strangely familiar to Erwin (a crumpled jacket lay behind his back), and a round metal box lay between his palms. Erwin reasoned that the man had died less than a month earlier and that the companions had taken his belongings but had not touched his bodies. When Philip again called him "a young man", Erwin threatened him with a sword in front of everyone. Further, the detachment found a cooled bonfire, stumps cut down with iron axes, and seven dugouts, in which twenty or thirty people wintered. Erwin concluded that there are people in the Beyond who are not known to any imperial treatise.

On the top of the hill, which turned out to be part of a gigantic earthen rampart, the detachment saw the failure of the steps three hundred feet across. The almost sheer walls were black as if burned, and the bottom was lost in the fog. The stone never hit the bottom. Erwin realized what was ahead of him:

“This cave, gentlemen, leads to the Underworld. We have found the Gift of the Gods.”

It was the bed of the uncounted Eighteenth Gift. Previously, the Gifts appeared in the empire seventeen times, less than once a century. By law, one-third of the Items of any Gift belonged to the Crown, and therefore Philip, useless until then, suddenly gained importance.

The death of the squad

On 8 June, the cayres descended into the bed. The descent was suspiciously facilitated by the similarity of the steps knocked out in the wall, and at the bottom there were only human bones and no Objects. Erwin realized that the heart of the lodge had been devastated before them and that the miners were the inhabitants of the dugouts. At dinner, to raise the spirit of the detachment, he made a speech: the gods seemed to send the Gift to the northerners, and the savages only extracted it for them. You need to find a village of savages, make them vassals of the Duke of Desmond, declare the "Blessed District" part of the Origin and take the Items.

At night, Louis called Erwin to the cliff, not sleeping, as if to show a faint blue shimmer in the depths. The mechanic explained that the shimmering Objects, according to churchmen, are deadly to sinful souls. While they were talking, the camp was attacked and Louis stabbed Erwin under the left collarbone. Erwin jumped off a cliff in the bed, fell on the ledge and crawled into the grotto, plugging the wound. On top of that, he heard Louis reporting to a man he called "cheese." He spoke with a weak accent, which Erwin could not recognize, reproached the mechanic that the lord should have been killed before the River, and something made Louis snort with pain; finally he threw: "Fragile, fragile man."

On the morning of June 9, Erwin climbed the same steps. The camp was littered with mutilated bodies: Oswald, Frederick, Matthew, Baron Philip, Tommy, who had already been bitten by a wolf. Among the dead was a stranger - a red-bearded warrior in a chain mail and a scarlet shirt, with a piece of a spark spear stick. The dying Theobart said that there were about thirty attackers and that they were not savages, but imperial spark infantry in red shirts, speaking with the accent of the Crown Lands. The captain told Erwin to write down everything, nail a note to a tree, and shoot himself from the crossbow. Erwin refused, repeating "I will survive", and left Teobarta his dagger. Soon Erwin heard a short groan, and there was silence.

Survival of the River

Erwin treated the wound with alcohol, took the medicine chest, crossbow and food and crawled into one of the dugouts. The wound was festering, he was tormented by fever and delusional dreams: a kiss with Nexia, a party in execution with General William Davey, childhood with Iona, a training fight with Richard. (William Davy) Remembering Kid’s lesson, he began to open the boil with a dagger and pour poisonous juice of snakes-grass into the wound, which animals treat wounds with. Each time he lost consciousness. At the same time he first appeared Agatha the Radiant. Erwin listed those he wanted revenge on: "Theobarth and Tommy, Kairs and Greys, Rain and Leocant."

When the food ran out, Erwin crawled out of the dugout and fell asleep at the meadow of snake-grass. When he woke up, he saw Sagittarius and Jemis above him. The exile followed the detachment to avenge his disgrace, but instead of revenge, he went out to the lord: he stitched up the wound, fed it and buried the dead. Later, Jemis admitted that he himself had tried the juice of snake grass on the cut and realized that Erwin had survived. He offered to serve, and Erwin agreed, but promised to return the cape only when Jemis proves himself worthy. Recovering, Erwin disassembled the evidence (scarlet shirts, boots with soft leather inserts and straps, which are massively sewn for the infantry, double spark spears) and concluded that the detachment was interrupted by Imperial infantry secretly developing an unaccounted for Dar.

Fort and Wilhelm's Fingers

On July 6, Erwin and Jemis and Sagittarius tracked down the log fort a day and a half away from the lodge. It was surrounded by a moat filled with water from the stream and a shaft, and on the shaft stood a twenty-foot wall with a gallery, loopholes and six square towers. Inside were two gates with lifting bridges, and wind blades were seen above the walls. The fortress occupied at least two acres.

Fifteen soldiers in scarlet shirts came out of the gate and brought out twelve emaciated bound captives. Their commander, Paul, lowered his fist into a pinkish-smoky quartz stone, which ran around his handcuffed, and in a moment burned one of the prisoners. Then he gave the same stone to the soldier, and the prisoners began to be released on the run, and the soldiers learned to fire on them. The last one to run was a shaved girl with burns on her head. She almost reached the hill where the Northmen were hiding, but Paul, with an invisible whistling force, first broke her legs, and then broke her whole body. Erwin fired a crossbow from about two hundred yards away, and the bolt lodged in Paul’s shoulder. A soldier with a floating disk in his eye saw the observers through the fern and burned the top of the hill. Running away, Erwin and Jemis named the weapon aloud: they were the Wilhelm's Fingers, which, according to legend, the Forefather Wilhelm drowned in the ocean.

Jemis led the chase to the bed, and Erwin went along the stream to the River. On the shore, he stumbled upon two soldiers, impersonated the recruit "Arthur the Skinny", sent by Paul, and, distracting them, stabbed them both. Under the knife, the wounded man admitted that he was serving the “lord”, and when asked whether Adrian, he shouted:

"Yes!.. We are serving the Emperor.”

Graveyard on the Cape

Crossing the River at sunset, Erwin led the horses to the cape, where the current carried the bodies of the dead in the fort. The cape was covered with a carpet of two hundred and three hundred rotting corpses, among which Erwin counted at least a dozen women and four children. People were dissected, burned, broke their bones, skinned and dried - just like the dead man at the ash. Erwin threw up. At night, the wolves picked up a trophy peg mare. Erwin waited for Jemis at the place of the previous crossing. He managed to warn the pursuers at the bed, but an invisible blow of Perst broke his sword and knocked his hand out of the joint.

Erwin showed Jemis the Cape of the Dead. Jemis recalled the siege of the pirate town of Hoyt on the Gran Islands, where everything was burned to the ground after the sea. Erwin replied that when they returned, they would do the same. He swore that to the east of the River there would be no people in scarlet shirts, no logs from their fort, no Subject. He added that whoever commands these people is not here.

Return

On the way back, Jemis taught the Lord every morning fencing with wooden swords. The fire burned a hole in the network of Soft Fields, and the travelers had to walk around the black water channel for three days. Jemis fell into the quagmire, Erwin was paralyzed for a day by a bite of a hare, the bird dragged away the remains of dried pork, and Jemis and Sagittarius ate the larvae (Erwin initially refused). There, Jemis admitted that he had heard Erwin's oath while still in the dugout, and called him a "bold gentle woman". Under Spot, they met Kid. Erwin told him only that the others were gone, refused to go into the village and sent a guy for food, and he waited at the Ice. Jemis threw in Kida's wake that all the tales of Zarechye are lies and don't even come close to truth.

On 30 August, on a slope above the First Winter, Erwin dedicated Jemis to kairs, naming him "Jemis Dorothy Laura of the Gloria family, Lord Lilliday" and putting a red and black cloak on his shoulders with his own hands. The sword of Jemis remained fragments at the bed, and he had to salute with a dagger. In the Cathedral of the Agatha the Radiant, Erwin sat in front of the fresco “The Decision of the Agatha the Radiant” and felt its answer: the main enemy is not in the Beyond, but stands so high that no faithful northern lord would raise a sword against him.

Aftermath

At the castle, Erwin learned that his father was struck by a stone disease and was ready to give him the title. Before the council, which included Earl Lilliday, Baron Statham, Colonels Horton and Blackberry, Duchess Sophia, Vittor and Iona, Erwin told everything he saw. Jemis confirmed his words and presented a spark spear and scarlet shirts of the dead. Erwin announced that the emperor had forced the Objects to speak and was preparing a blow to the Great Houses, and demanded either to judge him as a rebel or to overthrow Adrian. Desmond took an oath from his son not to doubt the guilt of the emperor, and Erwin became Duke of Origin. Soon the Northern War began. In the ultimatum, Adrian Erwin demanded to stop sacrilege in the Beyond, execute the guilty, release the prisoners and pay ten thousand ephes to the families of the victims.

Later, more was discovered. On September 10, 1774, Erwin instructed Jemis to go with the Earl of Fleming and three hundred warriors for the River to destroy the fort and find out how Adrian's men found Dar's bed: whether they were looking for it systematically or owned an Object that smells other Objects. In the fall, Fleming's flotilla with Mark and Jemis climbed the River. In the fort found a mountain of objects, insane prisoners Gwendoux and Louis. (Gwenda) Then the fort, along with a hundred northerners disappeared without a trace. Louis, who had been turned into a "goat" by torture, said that he had been told to kill Erwin before the River by the "man of the lord", the captain in the red, in the capital: he was captured, beaten and shown his beloved, beaten and burned with a candle, promising to spare her. Mark himself came to the conclusion that the fort was not Adrian or Erwin, but a third force. Later in the secret order Adrian explained the disappearance of the fort by the fact that the dozens of objects stored there from the Eighteenth Gift were destroyed and the spherical area, along with the fort, was “removed from the world”. In 1775, Erwin admitted publicly that the heretics with the Rings were not at the disposal of Adrian, but of the Puppeteer, with whom the emperor was only in alliance, "without understanding his powers." The puppeteer was Count Vittor Shayland, and the commander of his “brigade” was Paul. In presenting the case of the Church of the Foremothers in June 1775, Erwin argued that Shayland had appropriated the Eighteenth Gift, and Adrian had turned a blind eye to the atrocities of the brigade in exchange for the secret of the speaking Objects.

Trivia

  • The path of the exploit for the River and back are the first chapters of Arrow in the cycle. In them, Erwin turns from a metropolitan intriguer into a general.
  • The decision to cross the River, according to Erwin himself, was made to spite Baron Lowfert. Erwin later pondered what small accidents turn the wheels of history.
  • Passing the place of the previous crossing on the way back, Erwin remembered his words about the rafts. The island where they were traveling was the place where he met Jemis.
  • Later, while sailing to the River, Mark recounted the story of a mutiny in John-John's swamp, Gray Jemis, according to Hank the Sailor. Hank fled from the swamp, fearing revenge from the owner, hired a merchant schooner and spoke about the mutiny at the Crooked Bushprit at Two Rocks Bay. In this retelling, Jemis wanted not to remove, but to kill the Duke.

The Author's Word

  • According to the author, the hiking trip through the marshes was the Duke of Desmond's plan. (Desmond Origin) First, the expedition explored whether it was possible to lay the rails of the railway. Second, and most importantly, it was a test that should have made Erwin an adult. This would not have happened on the ship (stream on April 18, 2021).
  • According to the author, the burning of prisoners in the Beyond is evil without reservations (stream April 18, 2021).

In other words, the author’s word. (The Author's Word)
